mass_balance.crop_system: greenhouse tomato in rockwool, semi-closed and open soilless culture
mass_balance.ec_relation: EC = 0.19 + 0.095 * CAT, where CAT is charge-weighted Ca, K, Mg and Na concentration in mol/m3
important_assumptions: solution volumes remain approximately constant through replenishment and over-irrigation
substrate and tank/drain concentrations are treated as approximately equal
crop uptake concentration is stage dependent
the tested salinity range did not materially change leaf area, transpiration or nutrient uptake in that study

fresh_yield_ec_response.source_document: Li (2000), Analysis of greenhouse tomato production in relation to salinity and shoot environment

transpiration_regimes.low: targeted at 65% of high potential transpiration

limits: the two source transpiration regimes do not identify an arbitrary continuous response surface
cultivar and season differ from AGC 2019
mean campaign root-zone EC was used; this does not identify instantaneous EC stress
NaCl and concentrated nutrients at equal EC were not equivalent for marketable fresh yield
these curves must remain an external validity/sensitivity component until a transfer rule is preregistered

irrigation_policy_reference.crop_system: beefsteak greenhouse tomato in rockwool, spring-summer 2005
irrigation_policy_reference.design: randomized complete block, eight plots per treatment, four plants per plot

treatments.T1: irrigate at slab WC <=70% or slab EC >=1.4x seasonal feed EC
treatments.T2: irrigate at slab WC <=70% or slab EC >=1.7x seasonal feed EC
treatments.T3: irrigate at slab WC <=80% or slab EC >=1.4x seasonal feed EC
treatments.T4: irrigate at slab WC <=80% or slab EC >=1.7x seasonal feed EC
treatments.T5: irrigate after >=700 g combined plant-plus-slab weight loss
treatments.T6: irrigate after >=500 g combined plant-plus-slab weight loss

irrigation_policy_reference.reported_policy_ranking: T1, T2 and T6 had the strongest early and total marketable-yield pattern; T3, T4 and T5 were weaker
irrigation_policy_reference.mechanistic_interpretation: both excessive wetness with reduced root-zone oxygen and excessive dry-down can reduce performance
irrigation_policy_reference.use: external policy-ranking and plausible-operating-envelope check only
limits: water-content and EC triggers jointly determine four treatments, so they do not identify a continuous causal WC response
one instrumented plot controlled all eight replicate plots within each treatment
gas exchange was measured on one date and cannot identify dynamic stress parameters
thresholds are irrigation triggers rather than maintained slab-water-content setpoints
cultivar, season and greenhouse differ from AGC 2019

acute_drought_reference.crop_system: approximately one-year-old high-wire tomato in rockwool at Bleiswijk
acute_drought_reference.intervention: one three-plant slab had drip irrigation removed for 48 hours; one slab continued irrigation

observed_response.slab_water_content_m3_m3: approximately 0.4 to sensor floor 0.0 in 28 hours
observed_response.yield: not measured as a treatment outcome

acute_drought_reference.use: external acute-stress timing and sensor-observation check only
limits: one treated slab and one control slab; plant or leaf counts do not constitute independent treatment replicates
stopping fertigation also stopped nutrient delivery
near-complete dry-down is more severe than normal management
no identified crop-yield response or general dynamic conductance-versus-WC curve
stomatal response and stem recovery occurred on different timescales
